text: When working with APIs, you send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use in programming. Before making requests, you usually need authentication, like an API key, to prove who you are. This key is often included in the request header. It's also important to respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time. If you send too many, you may get an error. Good error handling means checking the response status and managing problems like network issues or invalid data smoothly. This helps your application stay reliable.
